resources.string: Read the Quran word by word, and follow a recitation as you listen.

The letters of each verse are coloured by the rule they are recited with, in the reading of Hafs from ‘Asim. Rules that depend on where the reciter stops follow the recording.
Letters read plainly (الإظهار), and ordinary long vowels written as full letters, keep the text\'s own colour.
an echo on a stopped letter
merged whole, or written and not said
A doubled n or m is held through the nose for two counts.
An n without a vowel, or a tanween, is hidden before any of fifteen letters (ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك): neither clear nor merged, with the nasal sound kept.
An m without a vowel is hidden before b, with the nasal sound kept.
An n without a vowel, or a tanween, turns into an m before b. The small م written over it marks this.
An n without a vowel, or a tanween, at the end of a word merges into y, n, m or w (ي ن م و) at the start of the next, through the nose.
An m without a vowel merges into the m after it, through the nose.
A long vowel before a doubled letter or one that never has a vowel, and the letters that open some surahs: always six counts.
A long vowel before a hamza in the same word: four or five counts.
A long vowel that ends a word, before a hamza that opens the next: four or five counts with Hafs, and two are allowed. It applies only when the reciter runs on.
The pronoun “hu” or “hi” before a hamza is drawn out like the munfasil.
A long vowel before the last letter of a word the reciter stops on: two, four or six counts.
A w or y without a vowel after a fatha, before the last letter of a word the reciter stops on: two, four or six counts.
The ordinary long vowel, two counts. It is coloured where the mushaf writes it with a small letter instead of a full one.
The pronoun “hu” or “hi” between two vowelled letters is drawn out two counts when the reciter runs on.
Stopping on a word that ends in “-an”: it is said as a long a, two counts.
The letters ق ط ب ج د without a vowel, or stopped on, are released with a slight echo. It is stronger at a stop.
An r is full-mouthed with a fatha or a damma, and without a vowel after one. With a kasra, or after one, it is light and keeps the text\'s colour.
The l of the name of Allah is full-mouthed after a fatha or a damma, and light after a kasra.
An n without a vowel, or a tanween, merges whole into l or r, with no nasal sound.
A letter without a vowel merges into the same letter after it.
A letter without a vowel merges into one said from the same place: ت د ط, ث ذ ظ, and ب into م.
A letter without a vowel merges into one said from close by: ل into ر, and ق into ك.
The l of “al-” before a sun letter is not said: the letter after it is doubled instead.
The joining alif is said only when a recitation begins with it, and is passed over when run into.
Letters the mushaf writes and the reciter does not say, marked with a small circle.
The download was interrupted. Try again to carry on from where it stopped.

Recite a verse to the phone. It listens, and marks what to go over again: a letter, a vowel, the length of a madd, a ghunnah.
“Adorn the Quran with your voices.” (Abu Dawud, al-Nasa\'i)
Tajweed comes first: a melody must never change a letter, a vowel or the length of a madd.
How long one breath carries a steady sound
Breathe in through the nose to a slow count of four, filling the belly. Then let the air out on one steady “aaah” for as long as is comfortable. Don\'t push to the last of your air.
Hold one note without letting it waver
Pick a note that is easy for you, neither low nor high, and hold it on “aaah” for five seconds or more. Watch the line and keep it level.
From your lowest easy note to your highest
Start on the lowest note that is still easy and slide slowly up to the highest that is still easy, without forcing. Reciters call the low end the qarar and the high end the jawab.
This needs the microphone. Allow it for this app in the phone\'s settings.
No voice was heard. Try again a little louder, closer to the phone.
Loudness swelled or faded: aim for one even level
How far the note strayed. A cent is a hundredth of a semitone.
It wavers: put more breath behind the note and less throat
The breath exercise is one recitation teachers give. Holding a note and sliding through the range are general voice exercises.
Stop if your throat feels strained or hoarse. Drink water, and carry the sound on your breath, not your throat.
Tap the microphone and recite this verse, stopping at its end. Up to half a minute at a time.
Tap a marked word to see what to go over.
This can be wrong. It is an aid for going over your recitation, not a teacher: take what it marks to someone who can listen to you.
Checking a recitation needs a small tajweed model (23 MB), fetched once and kept on the phone.
Nothing was heard. Recite a little louder, closer to the phone.

resources.string: It was held for %1$d counts and is due %2$d. Count at your own pace: a short vowel is one count, the natural madd two.
It was held for %1$d counts and is due %2$d. Counting at your own pace keeps every madd to its measure.
The vowel was said short. Here it is held for %1$d counts.
A vowel lengthened where there is no madd
A short vowel is one count. Stretching it turns it into a letter that isn\'t in the word.
In this recitation it was held for %1$s counts in turn. Whatever length you choose for it, keep that length every time.
A doubled ن or م carries a nasal sound that is held, about two counts. Let it ring through the nose before moving on.
Ikhfaʾ: the nun was said clearly
Before this letter the ن is hidden. Don\'t let the tongue touch its place: keep it just clear, and hold the nasal sound.
Ikhfaʾ: the nasal sound cut short
The hidden ن keeps its ghunnah. Hold the nasal sound before going on to the next letter.
Before ب the ن turns into a hidden م with ghunnah. Close the lips gently, without pressing, and hold the nasal sound.
Here the ن is not sounded: it merges into %1$s. Go straight to that letter and double it.
The ن merges into %1$s and its nasal sound stays. Hold that sound as you double the letter.
A letter with a shadda is said twice: rest on it, then release it into its vowel.
ق ط ب ج د without a vowel are let go with a slight echo. It is not a vowel: the mouth doesn\'t open or round for it. It is stronger at a stop.
A vowel changed is a clear mistake: it can change the word\'s meaning. Look at the sign on the letter and say it again slowly.
Every letter of the word is to be heard. Say the word slowly, sound by sound.
A sound was heard that the word doesn\'t have. Say the word slowly, sound by sound.
It was passed over, or said too softly to be heard. Recite the verse again and give the word its place.

string-array.name: letter_tips
string-array.item: ء comes from the deepest part of the throat, closed off sharply and kept light.
ه comes from the deepest part of the throat, light and breathy.
ع comes from the middle of the throat, squeezed. It is not a hamza.
ح comes from the middle of the throat, squeezed, with the breath running. It is not a ه.
غ comes from the top of the throat, where one gargles. It is not a hard g.
خ comes from the top of the throat. The tongue doesn\'t close on the palate as for ك.
ق is the deepest part of the tongue against the soft palate above it, heavy. It is not a ك.
ك is the back of the tongue, a little forward of ق, on the palate, light, with a little breath.
ج is the middle of the tongue against the palate, pressed and held. It is not a soft j.
ش is the middle of the tongue against the palate, with the air spreading in the mouth.
ي is the middle of the tongue against the palate.
ض is the side of the tongue against the upper molars, heavy, the sound running along it. It is not a د or a ظ.
ل is the front edges of the tongue up to its tip against the gums of the upper teeth, light.
ن is the tip of the tongue against the gum of the upper front teeth.
ر is the tip of the tongue, with a little of its top, tapping the gum once. Don\'t roll it on.
ط is the tip of the tongue at the roots of the upper front teeth with the tongue pressed up, heavy. It is not a ت.
د is the tip of the tongue at the roots of the upper front teeth, light.
ت is the tip of the tongue at the roots of the upper front teeth, light, with breath.
ص is the tip of the tongue toward the lower front teeth with the back of the tongue raised: heavy, with a whistle. It is not a س.
ز is the tip of the tongue toward the lower front teeth, voiced, with a whistle.
س is the tip of the tongue toward the lower front teeth, thin, with a whistle. It must not thicken into ص.
ظ is the tip of the tongue at the edges of the upper front teeth, heavy. It is not a z.
ذ is the tip of the tongue at the edges of the upper front teeth, light. It is not a z.
ث is the tip of the tongue at the edges of the upper front teeth, with breath. It is not a س.
ف is the inside of the lower lip against the edges of the upper front teeth.
ب is the two lips closed firmly, light.
م is the two lips closed, without pressing.
و is the two lips rounded.
